coordinates.object_orientation: Head -Y, tail+Y, up+Z; low grounded quadruped.

concept.reason: Published skeletal diagram visually inspected; no generated concept needed.

scope: Original whole organism with deep angular narrow head and robust limbs; not generic broad flat salamander or isolated skull.
specimen_basis: Primary Whitney et al.2022 Fig1 skeletal reconstruction and associated FMNH PR5021/1962/1958/5023 femora; these numbers identify femora, not the composite skeleton or skull. Rawson2021 CT skull study abstract supports exceptionally narrow skull and anterior fangs.

scale.basis: Artistic adult target within Field Museum reported6–6.5ft range, not exact measurement of named specimen. Skeleton reference10cm bar.

diagnostic_targets: Deep angular wedge-like narrow skull, not a pancake-wide temnospondyl head; distinct cheek and long jaw with restrained anterior fangs.
Stout shoulders and hips with four robust bent limbs and grounded feet; moderate trunk and relatively short tapering tail, not eel-like proportions.
Keep cranial sensory grooves subtle; no external gills, crocodilian armor, frog body or mammalian ears.
uncertainties: Skin colour, tissue thickness, pose and visible digit detail are artistic; do not label exact soft tissue or toe count fossil-proven.
Composite whole-body diagram is a scientific reconstruction, not photograph of one complete specimen.
Museum image and UCL fullPDF downloads403, not visually inspected; body diagram available and inspected.
acceptance_checks: Side shows deep head profile; top shows narrow elongated head rather than broad disc.
Four robust attached limbs, no floating toes, no extremely long aquatic whip-tail.
All four standard views readable, no extra render suite or concept images.
Original procedural geometry/materials; research figure excluded public deliverable.
handoff_contract: Same localdir prep/maker/QA; maker sends fixedhash COMPLETE. Root asynchronous backup, local retained for integration. No upload or cleanup by maker.
